Patient note:
A 45-year-old right-hand–dominant male was referred from his primary care office for preoperative cardiovascular risk stratification after discovery of a small enhancing 2.4-cm mass at the lower pole of the left kidney on imaging obtained for intermittent flank discomfort; cross-sectional scans and bone survey reveal no evidence of regional nodal involvement, vascular invasion, or distant spread, and he has not yet undergone any ablative or surgical therapy. His past medical history is notable for a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction occurring three years earlier while he was shoveling snow; at that time coronary angiography demonstrated a discrete 90 % lesion in the mid-left anterior descending artery that was treated with a drug-eluting stent, and he completed dual antiplatelet therapy without recurrent ischemia. He reports no exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, lower-extremity edema, or rapid weight gain, and on today’s examination jugular venous pressure is not elevated, lung fields are clear, there are no added heart sounds or murmurs, and distal pulses are symmetric and bounding. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus six years ago during routine screening when his fasting plasma glucose measured 142 mg/dL; glycemic control has since been maintained with metformin 1000 mg twice daily, diet, and regular exercise, with his most recent hemoglobin A1c last month reported at 7.1 %. Surveillance labs have shown normal creatinine, an estimated glomerular filtration rate consistently above 90 mL/min/1.73 m², and a urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio within reference limits; monofilament testing at the feet is normal and dilated retinal exam last year was unremarkable, indicating absence of end-organ sequelae. He denies any prior cerebrovascular events, transient neurologic deficits, seizures, focal weakness, or speech disturbances, and neurologic examination is intact with normal strength, sensation, and coordination. He also denies chronic cough, wheezing, exercise-induced bronchospasm, or prior need for bronchodilators, and spirometry performed as part of his occupational screening two years ago demonstrated normal FEV1/FVC. There is no history of connective tissue disorders, inflammatory arthropathy, photosensitivity rashes, oral ulcers, or serositis; he is likewise without history of chronic epigastric pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, melena, or prior endoscopy suggesting mucosal ulceration. His liver panel is within normal ranges, he has never had jaundice, ascites, encephalopathy, or portal signs, and he consumes alcohol only socially, averaging one to two beers on weekends. He is HIV-negative on a screening test performed last year, denies intravenous drug use, and has had no opportunistic infections. Surgical history is limited to an uncomplicated appendectomy at age 18. Current medications include low-dose aspirin, metformin, high-intensity atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, and a daily angiotensin receptor blocker for blood-pressure control, with home readings averaging 122/76 mm Hg. He does not use tobacco and has a body mass index of 28 kg/m². Family history is significant for premature coronary artery disease in his father at age 54 and breast cancer in a maternal aunt; there is no family history of stroke, peripheral arterial disease, or connective tissue disease. On presentation today, vital signs are: temperature 36.8 °C, blood pressure 128/78 mm Hg in the right arm seated, heart rate 68 beats per minute regular, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 98 % on ambient air. Cardiac auscultation reveals a normal S1 and S2 without gallop or murmur; lungs are clear; abdomen is soft and nontender with no palpable masses or organomegaly; there is no peripheral edema or calf tenderness. Laboratory data from this morning show hemoglobin 15.1 g/dL, white blood cell count 6.2 × 10⁹/L, platelet count 235 × 10⁹/L, sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.3 mmol/L, bicarbonate 24 mmol/L, BUN 14 mg/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, AST 24 U/L, ALT 27 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 66 U/L, total bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, fasting glucose 126 mg/dL, and lipid panel showing LDL 61 mg/dL. Urinalysis is clear with trace protein, no hematuria. An electrocardiogram demonstrates normal sinus rhythm with Q waves in the anterior leads consistent with prior infarction but no acute changes, and a transthoracic echocardiogram performed last month for routine follow-up showed left ventricular ejection fraction of 60 % with normal wall-motion except a mild anteroseptal hypokinesis, no valvular abnormalities, and normal right ventricular size and function. The patient seeks clearance for elective partial nephrectomy, and the current evaluation summarizes his cardiovascular and metabolic status prior to any oncologic or surgical intervention.

Question: What is the patient's Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) sums weighted comorbidities present before surgery. Age adjustment adds no points before age 50.
- Age 45: 0.
- Prior myocardial infarction: the documented NSTEMI counts despite successful stenting: +1.
- Diabetes without end-organ damage: no documented nephropathy, neuropathy, or retinopathy: +1.
- Localized solid tumor: the renal mass is scored as a nonmetastatic tumor (+2), not metastatic disease (+6).
- No other qualifying condition, including heart failure or moderate-to-severe renal disease: 0.
Total: 0 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 0 = 4.
Final answer: 4
